# Architecture

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate_documents.py; edit source records instead. -->


## One source per kind of knowledge

### Decision

Requests, decisions and rules are independently reviewable Markdown records with a `status` field in YAML-style front matter. Only `approved` requests, `accepted` decisions and `active` rules appear in generated documents. Files are assembled in lexical filename order.

Derived Markdown files are committed for easy discovery and GitHub rendering, but are not independently edited. A dependency-free generator produces them deterministically, and CI rejects stale outputs. Root human-facing entrypoints are real Git symlinks to the derived documents.

### Rationale

This prevents drift between duplicate READMEs, contribution guides, architecture summaries and approved requirements without requiring a specific language runtime beyond Python 3 for repository automation. Changes remain reviewable at the source-record level.

### Consequences

Editing a source record requires regeneration of its derived document in the same change. Draft or superseded records remain in place for history but are excluded from current projections.

_Source: [0001-single-document-source.md](decisions/0001-single-document-source.md)_


## Development integration and release

### Decision

The `development` branch is the integration branch; `main` is the release branch. Feature work targets `development`. A merge into `main` must originate from `development` and pass required checks and review. Release versions use the root `VERSION` file as their sole source.

For a same-repository pull request, automation creates one version-bump commit on its head branch, using the next patch version greater than either the base or head version. A distinct `v<version>` tag and GitHub Release are created by automation for each new commit landing on `main`. Existing tags must never be moved.

### Rationale

Separate integration and release lanes prevent ordinary feature PRs from directly entering the release branch. Version commits in the PR branch keep the chosen release number reviewable; tagging on `main` avoids releasing unmerged code.

### Consequences

GitHub branch protection must be configured in repository settings to make workflow checks genuinely mandatory. The workflow source-branch guard is an additional check, not a replacement for protection. Fork pull requests cannot receive automatic head-branch commits with the repository token, and must update their version manually.

_Source: [0002-development-and-release.md](decisions/0002-development-and-release.md)_
